300: The Darwin Incident by Shun Umezawa (Kodansha) is a tense, thoughtful thriller about what it means to be human. Charlie is a "humanzee," born to a chimpanzee rescued in a raid by animal rights activists. Raised by a kind human couple, he starts high school as an outsider with a sharp mind. When an extremist group sets its sights on him, his quiet life is pulled into danger. It's a smart pick for readers who like big ethical questions.
302: NG Life by Mizuho Kusanagi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted reincarnation romantic comedy. High school student Keidai Saeki remembers his past life in ancient Pompeii, where he was happily married. The trouble is that his beloved wife has been reborn as a boy, and his old best friend has come back as a girl. Keidai is left sorting out who he loves now. It's a funny, sweet read for fans of tangled shojo romance.
303: Hands Off by Kasane Katsumoto (Tokyopop) is a gentle supernatural mystery with a warm heart. Kotarou is a cheerful boy whose touch strengthens the psychic powers of the people around him. His cousin Tatsuki has abilities of his own, and together they keep stumbling into strange cases that need solving. The friendship between them anchors every story. It suits readers who like quiet, character-driven mysteries with a touch of the paranormal.
304: Happy Cafe by Kou Matsuzuki (Tokyopop) is a sweet, silly workplace comedy. Uru Ichiyama is small, cute, and surprisingly strong. When her mother remarries, Uru decides to give the newlyweds space and takes a live-in job at Cafe Bonheur. There she works alongside a grumpy pastry chef and a sleepy coworker who keeps dozing off. It's a cozy read for fans of found family and gentle romance.
305: Headhunted to Another World: From Salaryman to Big Four! by Benigashira (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy about office skills in a monster world. An overworked Japanese salaryman is suddenly recruited by a demon lord's army to serve as one of its four top generals. He has no magic to speak of, just years of real-world business sense. It's a fun read for anyone who has ever survived a tough job and wondered how that would work against heroes.
306: Ninja Girls by Hosana Tanaka (Kodansha) is a goofy action comedy set in feudal Japan. Raizo is a boy with an unfortunate face and a hidden past as the heir to a fallen clan. When a skilled young kunoichi named Kagari swears to protect him, he finds himself with a growing group of ninja allies. Together they set out to restore his family's lost land. It's light, playful fun for fans of slapstick and sword fights.
307: Battle Angel Alita by Yukito Kishiro (Kodansha) is a gritty science fiction action story. In a scrapyard beneath a floating city, the cyber-doctor Daisuke Ido finds the head of a cyborg girl and rebuilds her. Alita wakes with no memory, but her body remembers a deadly martial art. She becomes a bounty hunter while searching for who she really is. It's a classic for readers who like cyberpunk worlds and a lead with real heart.
309: Highschool of the Dead by Daisuke Sato and Shouji Sato (Yen Press) is a fast, violent zombie survival story. One ordinary school day, the dead start rising, and Takashi Komuro's high school falls into chaos within minutes. He gathers a small band of classmates and a school nurse to fight their way out and find their families. It's for older teens and adults who like nonstop action, gore, and plenty of fan service.
310: The Idaten Deities Know Only Peace by Amahara (Seven Seas) is a dark, often violent fantasy action story. Hundreds of years ago, the godlike Idaten wiped out the demons and brought peace to the world. A new generation of Idaten has grown up knowing nothing but that peace. When demons begin to return, these untested gods must decide how far they will go to protect humanity. It's for mature readers who like brutal, morally gray action.
311: Honey So Sweet by Amu Meguro (Viz Media) is a warm, tender high school romance. Nao Kogure is a shy girl who is terrified of Taiga Onise, a boy with bleached hair and a scary scowl. Then Taiga suddenly asks her to date him with marriage in mind. Nao slowly learns he is gentle, honest, and devoted underneath it all. It's a lovely pick for readers who like sweet, slow-building romance with kind characters.
313: The Moon on a Rainy Night by Kuzushiro (Kodansha) is a quiet, heartfelt yuri romance. High school student Saki Kaneda finds herself drawn to Kanon, a cool, beautiful classmate who is hard of hearing. As the two grow closer, Saki learns more about Kanon's world and how to truly listen to her. It's a gentle, thoughtful love story for readers who enjoy soft romance and careful portrayals of disability.
314: The Most Notorious "Talker" Runs the World's Greatest Clan by Yamorichan (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action story about brains over brawn. Noel Stollen dreams of becoming the strongest hunter, just like his legendary grandfather. The problem is that he was born a Talker, a support class seen as the weakest of all. Noel decides to rise anyway, using strategy, nerve, and a sharp tongue. It's fun for readers who like clever, scheming heroes.
315: I Got Caught Up in a Hero Summons by Toudai (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy comedy. Kaito Miyama is an ordinary young man who gets pulled into another world by accident when a real hero is summoned. With no special mission, he settles in to enjoy everyday life there. Somehow, though, he keeps catching the attention of the world's most powerful beings. It's a relaxed, feel-good read for fans of gentle isekai stories.
317: Blood Lad by Yuuki Kodama (Yen Press) is a playful action comedy set in the demon world. Staz is a vampire who runs his turf with ease but would rather spend his time obsessing over Japanese anime and games. When a human girl named Fuyumi wanders into his territory, he is thrilled, until she is killed and turns into a ghost. Staz vows to bring her back to life. It's goofy, stylish fun with plenty of fights.
318: The Saint's Magic Power Is Omnipotent by Yuka Tachibana (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy romance. Sei is a hardworking office worker who is summoned to another world to serve as its Saint, only to be ignored in favor of a younger girl summoned with her. Rather than sulk, Sei takes a job at a research institute making potions. Her work turns out to be far more powerful than anyone expected. It's a calm, cozy read with a capable heroine.
320: I'm the Evil Lord of an Intergalactic Empire! by Yomu Mishima (Seven Seas) is a science fiction comedy with plenty of action. After a miserable life, Liam is reborn as the heir to a noble house in a vast space empire. This time he plans to be a selfish, wicked lord who takes what he wants. Somehow, every scheme he tries makes his people happier and his lands stronger. It's fun for readers who enjoy a hero who misreads his own story.
321: The Story of Saiunkoku by Sai Yukino and Kairi Yura (Viz Media) is a graceful historical fantasy. Shurei Hong comes from a noble family but has grown up poor, and she dreams of serving in government, a path closed to women. Then she is offered a large sum to enter the palace as a consort and teach a lazy young emperor how to rule. It's a smart, warm read for fans of court intrigue and a determined heroine.
324: In the Clear Moonlit Dusk by Mika Yamamori (Kodansha) is a sweet high school romance. Yoi Kurosaki is tall and handsome, so her classmates have always treated her like a prince instead of a girl. Then she meets Ichimura, an older student who is also called a prince, and he treats her as a girl from the very first moment. Yoi isn't sure what to make of it. It's a gentle read for fans of heartfelt shojo romance.
329: Pokémon Adventures: Black and White by Hidenori Kusaka and Satoshi Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a fun, fast-paced adventure for young readers. Black is a boy with one big dream: to win the Pokémon League. Along the way he teams up with White, a girl who runs a talent agency for Pokémon. Their journey across the Unova region is full of battles, new Pokémon, and a mysterious group called Team Plasma. It's a great fit for kids who love the games.
330: Chobits by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a sweet, thoughtful science fiction romance. Hideki is a struggling student in Tokyo who can't afford a persocom, the humanlike computers everyone seems to own. One night he finds one lying in a pile of trash and takes her home. She can only say one word, so he names her Chi. As he teaches her about the world, he begins to wonder what she really is. It's charming and quietly moving.
331: Chrono Crusade by Daisuke Moriyama (ADV) is a supernatural action story set in 1920s America. Sister Rosette Christopher is a hot-headed nun who fights demons for the Magdalan Order, usually causing as much damage as she prevents. Her partner is Chrono, a gentle-looking boy who is secretly a demon. Together they hunt evil while chasing a personal mission tied to Rosette's lost brother. It's exciting and emotional, with a great historical setting.
332: Princess Jellyfish by Akiko Higashimura (Kodansha) is a warm, funny comedy about finding your people. Tsukimi is a shy young woman obsessed with jellyfish who lives in a Tokyo boarding house full of fellow female otaku who avoid stylish people at all costs. One night she meets a glamorous fashionista who helps her save a jellyfish, and who turns out to be a young man in disguise. It's a delight for anyone who has ever felt out of place.
333: Tokyo Tarareba Girls by Akiko Higashimura (Kodansha) is a funny, honest comedy about adult life and love. Rinko is a thirty-three-year-old screenwriter who spends her nights drinking with her two best friends and talking about what might have been. When a handsome younger man bluntly calls them out, the three women are forced to look hard at their lives. It's sharp, relatable, and a great fit for readers who like grown-up romantic comedy.
335: Rasetsu by Chika Shiomi (Viz Media) is a supernatural romance with plenty of action. Rasetsu Hyuga is a cheerful, sweets-loving exorcist with a dangerous secret. A demon marked her years ago and will come to claim her when she turns twenty, unless she finds true love first. She works at an agency that clears out evil spirits, alongside a team with their own complicated pasts. It's a lively read for fans of ghost stories and romance.
339: Kingdom Hearts II by Shiro Amano (Yen Press) is a lighthearted adventure based on the video game. Roxas is spending the last days of summer vacation in Twilight Town with his friends, but strange dreams about a boy named Sora keep breaking through. Odd things begin happening around town, and Roxas starts to suspect his world isn't what it seems. It's a fun, easy read for kids and longtime fans of the games and Disney characters.
340: Kiss of the Rose Princess by Aya Shouoto (Viz Media) is a fantasy romance with a playful streak. Anis Yamamoto has always worn a choker her father gave her, and she was warned that something bad would happen if she ever took it off. When it comes loose, she ends up with four handsome Rose Knights bound to serve her. The catch is that she has to kiss them to call on their powers. It's fun for fans of reverse-harem romance.
341: Date A Live by Koushi Tachibana (Yen Press) is a science fiction romantic comedy with plenty of action. High school student Shido Itsuka gets caught up in a spacequake and meets a Spirit, a powerful girl whose appearances wreck entire cities. A secret group recruits him with an unusual plan: instead of fighting the Spirits, Shido must date them and make them fall in love with him. It's for readers who enjoy harem comedy and big battles.
342: Venus Versus Virus by Atsushi Suzumi (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action story. Sumire Suzuki has always been able to see Viruses, monsters invisible to almost everyone else. When one attacks her, she is saved by Lucia, a girl who runs a secret shop called Venus Vanguard and fights these creatures. Sumire soon joins the battle herself. It's a solid pick for readers who like monster hunting and a strong friendship between two very different girls.
343: Saiyuki by Kazuya Minekura (Tokyopop) is a stylish action fantasy loosely based on Journey to the West. A mysterious force has driven the demons of the land into a violent frenzy. The foul-mouthed priest Genjo Sanzo is ordered to travel west and stop it, with three unlikely companions: the cheerful Goku, the flirt Gojyo, and the polite Hakkai. It's full of banter, gunfights, and wounded hearts, and a favorite for fans of road-trip adventures.
344: Life by Keiko Suenobu (Tokyopop) is a raw, serious drama about bullying and survival. Ayumu is a high school girl who copes with stress by hurting herself. When she befriends a popular classmate, Manami, it seems like things might get better, but the friendship turns into a target. The story deals frankly with self-harm and cruelty among teens. It's a powerful read for older readers ready for difficult subjects, with a story about finding the strength to stand up.
347: Lone Wolf and Cub by Kazuo Koike and Goseki Kojima (Dark Horse) is a classic samurai drama. Ogami Itto was the shogun's executioner until he was framed by a rival clan and his wife was murdered. Now he walks the path of an assassin for hire, pushing his toddler son Daigoro in a wooden cart. Each chapter brings a new job and a new look at Edo-era Japan. It's a landmark series for adult readers who like historical action.
348: Yakuza Fiancé by Asuka Konishi (Seven Seas) is a sharp, intense romantic drama. Yoshino Somei is the granddaughter of a powerful yakuza boss who just wants a normal high school life. Then she is engaged to Kirishima Miyama, the charming heir of another crime family. He's polite and handsome, but it quickly becomes clear that something about him is deeply unsettling. It's for older readers who like dangerous romance and complicated characters.
350: Magic Knight Rayearth by CLAMP (Kodansha) is a classic magical fantasy adventure. Hikaru, Umi, and Fuu are three junior high girls who meet by chance on a school trip to Tokyo Tower. Suddenly they are pulled into the world of Cephiro, where Princess Emeraude has called them to become legendary Magic Knights and save her land. It's a colorful, heartfelt story about friendship and courage, and a great entry point to CLAMP's work.
351: Magic Touch by Izumi Tsubaki (Viz Media) is a light, funny high school romantic comedy. Chiaki Togu is a quiet girl who belongs to her school's massage club and takes her craft very seriously. Her dream is to work on the perfect back, and she finds it on Yosuke Moriyama, a popular boy who has no interest in being anyone's practice partner. It's charming, low-stakes fun from the creator of Monthly Girls' Nozaki-kun.
352: Your and My Secret by Ai Morinaga (ADV) is a quirky body-swap comedy. Akira is a gentle, shy boy with a crush on Nanako, a beautiful classmate with a rude and rowdy personality. When an invention made by Nanako's grandfather goes wrong, the two of them end up in each other's bodies. Now Akira has to live as a girl, while Nanako cheerfully enjoys life as a boy. It's an offbeat, funny look at gender and expectations.
353: Yu-Gi-Oh! GX by Naoyuki Kageyama (Viz Media) is a fun card-battle action comedy based on Kazuki Takahashi's Yu-Gi-Oh! Jaden Yuki is a cheerful, confident duelist who enrolls at Duel Academy, a school dedicated to the card game Duel Monsters. He makes friends and rivals while working his way up through tough duels and strange mysteries on campus. It's an easy, energetic read for kids and fans of the anime and card game.
354: Everyone's Getting Married by Izumi Miyazono (Viz Media) is a grown-up romantic comedy. Asuka Takanashi has a great career, but what she wants most is to get married and build a home. When her longtime boyfriend says no to marriage, she ends up meeting Ryu Nanami, a popular newscaster who has no plans to marry, ever. The two clash over what they want from life. It's a thoughtful, honest romance for adult readers.
355: Mardock Scramble by Tow Ubukata and Yoshitoki Oima (Kodansha) is a dark science fiction crime thriller. Rune Balot is a young woman who is nearly murdered by the man who took her in. She is saved by a scientist and brought back as a cyborg with the power to control electronics. With the help of Oeufcoque, a talking mouse who can transform into any tool, she seeks justice. It's for mature readers who like intense, gritty stories.
358: Kirby Manga Mania by Hirokazu Hikawa (Viz Media) is a silly, cheerful comedy for young readers. Kirby is a round, pink hero with a huge appetite who lives in peaceful Dream Land. In short, gag-filled stories, he gets into trouble with King Dedede, Meta Knight, and plenty of other familiar faces from the games. It's full of slapstick and goofy jokes, and a great choice for kids or anyone who loves Kirby.
360: If It's for My Daughter, I'd Even Defeat a Demon Lord by CHIROLU (J-Novel Club) is a warm, gentle fantasy about family. Dale is a skilled young adventurer who finds a small demon girl named Latina alone in the forest. She is wearing a mark of punishment and has nowhere to go, so he takes her home. Before long, the tough adventurer is a doting dad. It's a cozy slice-of-life read for fans of found family.
362: Life with an Ordinary Guy Who Reincarnated into a Total Fantasy Knockout by Yu Tsurusaki (Seven Seas) is a funny fantasy romantic comedy. Hinata and his best friend Tsukasa are thirtysomething office workers who get pulled into another world together. There's one twist: Hinata now has the body of a stunning young woman. As they set out on their adventure, Tsukasa starts to have very confusing feelings. It's light, silly fun with a sweet heart.
363: Reborn! by Akira Amano (Viz Media) is an action comedy that starts silly and grows into a big battle story. Tsuna Sawada is a middle schooler who is bad at sports, bad at school, and bad at talking to his crush. Then a baby hitman named Reborn arrives with news: Tsuna is next in line to lead a powerful mafia family. Reborn is there to whip him into shape. It's a favorite for fans of shonen action and friendship.
364: Asadora! by Naoki Urasawa (Viz Media) is a sweeping drama with a mystery at its core. In 1959 Nagoya, Asa Asada is a spirited girl from a big family who gets lost in the chaos of a deadly typhoon. During the disaster she meets a gruff former pilot, and he teaches her to fly. Years later, Japan faces a strange new threat. It's a thoughtful, page-turning read from the creator of Monster and 20th Century Boys.
365: Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree by Nikiichi Tobita (Yen Press) is a gag comedy based on the hit video game. A clumsy, weak Tarnished sets out across the Lands Between to become Elden Lord, and fails often. He dies, comes back, gets lost, and runs into the game's familiar bosses and characters along the way. It's a funny, affectionate take on the game, best for players who know the pain of trying again.
366: Firefly Wedding by Oreco Tachibana (Viz Media) is a romantic period drama set in Meiji-era Japan. Satoko is the frail daughter of a wealthy family who is not expected to live long, and she longs to marry before that day comes. When an assassin named Shinpei is hired to kill her, Satoko makes him an unexpected offer. What follows is a tense, dangerous romance. It's a lovely pick for fans of historical love stories with an edge.
368: Yakuza Fiancé by Asuka Konishi (Seven Seas) is a sharp, intense romantic drama. Yoshino Somei is the granddaughter of a powerful yakuza boss who just wants a normal high school life. Then she is engaged to Kirishima Miyama, the charming heir of another crime family. He's polite and handsome, but it quickly becomes clear that something about him is deeply unsettling. It's for older readers who like dangerous romance and complicated characters.
369: Saving 80,000 Gold in Another World for My Retirement by FUNA (Kodansha) is a cheerful fantasy comedy. After losing her family, Mitsuha Yamano discovers she can travel back and forth between Earth and a fantasy world. She decides to put that power to work, trading goods between worlds to save enough gold to retire comfortably. Things rarely stay simple for long. It's fun for readers who like clever, practical heroines and plenty of humor.
371: Too Many Losing Heroines! by Takibi Amamori and Imigimuru (Seven Seas) is a funny romantic comedy. Kazuhiko Nukumizu is a quiet, unremarkable high school student who likes to keep to himself. Then he overhears his popular classmate Anna Yanami getting turned down by the boy she likes. Soon he is the unofficial listener for one heartbroken girl after another. It's a light, clever read for fans of school comedy with lots of heart.
372: Easygoing Territory Defense by the Optimistic Lord by Sou Akaike (Seven Seas) is a relaxed fantasy about building a better home. Van is the young son of a noble family who is given Production Magic, a skill everyone considers useless. Sent off to rule a tiny, struggling village, he quickly learns his magic can build almost anything. Bit by bit, he turns his little territory into something remarkable. It's a cozy read for fans of town-building stories.
374: Ascendance of a Bookworm Part 2 by Miya Kazuki and Suzuka (J-Novel Club) continues a gentle fantasy about loving books. Myne, once a book-obsessed college student, was reborn as a sickly girl in a world where books are rare and costly. In Part 2, she enters the temple as an apprentice shrine maiden, where she finally gains access to a library. New rules and new responsibilities come with it. It's a warm, thoughtful read for readers who enjoy patient worldbuilding.
375: Campfire Cooking in Another World with My Absurd Skill by Ren Eguchi and Akagishi K (J-Novel Club) is a cozy fantasy comedy about food. Mukohda is an ordinary salaryman who gets summoned to another world by accident. His only skill lets him buy groceries from a modern Japanese supermarket. His home-cooked meals soon win over Fel, a legendary wolf who decides to follow him for the food. It's a relaxed, tasty read for fans of gentle isekai.
378: Senpai Is an Otokonoko by Pom (Kodansha) is a sweet romantic comedy about being yourself. Makoto Hanaoka is a cute upperclassman who loves wearing girls' clothes and keeps it a secret from most people. When a cheerful underclassman named Saki confesses her feelings, Makoto has to explain the truth. Meanwhile, a childhood friend has feelings of his own. It's a warm, thoughtful story about identity and love.
379: 10 Dance by Inouesatoh (Kodansha) is a passionate romance set in the world of competitive ballroom. Shinya Suzuki is a champion of Latin dance, and Shinya Sugiki is a champion of standard ballroom. The two rivals agree to teach each other their styles so they can both compete in the ten-dance event. Long hours of close practice turn into something far more complicated. It's for adult readers who like sports drama and slow-burn BL.
380: 7th Garden by Mitsu Izumi (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy action story. Awyn Gardner is a humble servant who only cares about tending the garden and serving the kind young lady of the house. When disaster strikes his village, a demon named Vyrde offers him the power to protect what he loves, at a steep price. Awyn accepts and is pulled into a war against angels. It's for readers who like grim fantasy with intense battles.
381: Steam Detectives by Kia Asamiya (Viz Media) is a stylish science fiction mystery. In a steam-powered city wrapped in smoke, young Narutaki is a boy detective who takes on the strangest cases in town. He works with Ling Ling, a nurse with a fighting spirit, and Goriki, a giant robot. Together they face villains in a world full of gears, gadgets, and old-fashioned adventure. It's a fun pick for steampunk and detective fans.
382: Fushigi Yûgi by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a classic fantasy romance. Miaka Yuki is a cheerful middle school student studying for entrance exams. While visiting the library, she finds a strange old book and is pulled into its world, a land based on ancient China. There she is named the Priestess of Suzaku and must gather seven celestial warriors. It's an emotional, sweeping adventure and a cornerstone of shojo manga.
383: Midori Days by Kazurou Inoue (Viz Media) is a sweet, silly romantic comedy. Seiji Sawamura is a tough guy who can't get a girlfriend because everyone is afraid of him. One morning he wakes up to find that his right hand has turned into a tiny girl named Midori, who has had a crush on him for ages. Now the two of them have to figure out daily life together. It's an odd, heartwarming story.
384: ACCA: 13-Territory Inspection Dept. by Natsume Ono (Yen Press) is a quiet, stylish mystery. Jean Otus is the second-in-command of ACCA's inspection department, a sleepy office that audits branches across a peaceful kingdom made up of thirteen territories. He mostly smokes, eats cake, and does his job. Then rumors of a coup begin to spread, and Jean finds himself at the center of them. It's a slow, smart read for fans of political intrigue.
385: Accomplishments of the Duke's Daughter by Reia (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance with a businesslike heroine. Iris realizes she is living as the villainess of an otome game at the very moment the prince publicly dumps her. Instead of accepting disgrace, she heads home and takes over managing her family's territory. Using her knowledge from her past life, she starts making real improvements. It's satisfying for readers who like smart, capable leads.
386: Sword Art Online: Girls' Ops by Reki Kawahara and Neko Nekobyou (Yen Press) is a lighthearted spin-off of the popular series. Lisbeth, Silica, and Leafa are best friends who play together in the virtual world of ALfheim Online. When a new player named Lux joins them, the girls form their own party and take on quests just for themselves. It's an easy, cheerful read for fans who want more time with SAO's supporting cast.
387: Air Gear by Oh!Great (Kodansha) is a high-energy action sports story. Itsuki "Ikki" Minami is a scrappy street fighter who discovers Air Treks, motorized inline skates that let riders race, leap, and battle across the city. He throws himself into the world of rival skating teams. Soon he is chasing the legend of the sky itself. It's packed with dazzling art and big fights, and a great pick for older teen readers who like adrenaline.
388: Gangsta by Kohske (Viz Media) is a gritty, hard-edged crime drama. In the lawless city of Ergastulum, Worick and Nicolas are handymen who take on jobs from the mob and the police alike. Nicolas is a deaf swordsman with a mysterious past, while Worick handles the talking. When they take in a former sex worker named Alex, their lives become even more complicated. It's for mature readers who like violent, character-driven noir.
390: Monkey High! by Shouko Akira (Viz Media) is a sweet high school romance. Haruna Aizawa transfers to a new school after a political scandal involving her family. To her, the school feels like a zoo full of noisy monkeys. Then she meets Macharu, a short, cheerful boy who doesn't care about her family's reputation. It's a gentle, funny love story for readers who enjoy classic shojo.
391: My Deer Friend Nokotan by Oshioshio (Seven Seas) is an absurd, high-energy comedy. Torako Koshi is a model student who is desperately hiding her past as a delinquent. Her secret is in danger when she meets Noko Shikanoko, a strange new classmate with deer antlers growing from her head. Nothing about Noko makes sense, and that's the joke. It's pure silliness for readers who like random humor and wild energy.
392: Alice in the Country of Hearts by QuinRose and Soumei Hoshino (Tokyopop) is a playful, slightly dark fantasy romance. Alice Liddell is a practical young woman who is kidnapped by a man with rabbit ears and dragged into Wonderland. This version is full of handsome, gun-toting residents, and many of them are interested in her. To get home, she must spend time getting to know them. It's for readers who like twisty fairy tales and reverse-harem romance.
394: Tenshi Ja Nai by Takako Shigematsu (Go! Comi) is a fun romantic comedy. Hikaru Mori is thrilled to be starting at an all-girls boarding school. Her roommate turns out to be a famous teen idol, which seems exciting until Hikaru discovers the idol is actually a boy in disguise. Now she is stuck keeping his secret. It's a playful, lighthearted read for fans of cross-dressing comedy and schoolyard romance.
395: Godchild by Kaori Yuki (Viz Media) is a gothic mystery set in Victorian London. Earl Cain Hargreaves is a young nobleman with a dark family history and a passion for poisons. Along with his loyal servant Riff and his little sister Mary Weather, he investigates strange crimes among London's high society. It's moody, elegant, and twisted, a great fit for readers who like dark fairy tales and period mysteries.
396: My Hero Academia: Team-Up Missions by Yoko Akiyama (Viz Media) is a cheerful spin-off of Kohei Horikoshi's series. To help young heroes grow, the pro-hero world starts a program that pairs students with surprising partners. Each mission brings together different combinations of heroes and students, from familiar faces to fan favorites. The stories are short, funny, and full of action. It's a great extra for fans who want more time with the whole cast.
